Do not return hashes; the host binds immutable hashes.", "context": {"title": "David Copperfield", "unit": 27, "heading": "CHAPTER 25. GOOD AND BAD ANGELS", "previous_rows": [{"source_id": "en85-u027-b0030", "target": "— А когда, Агнес, — спросил я, — ты простишь мне тот вечер?", "source_sha256": "99c2b574eb653b90bbeb75404c74b4cc38a820e06a2560df20b9bf38de8914a6", "target_id": "ru-en85-u027-b0030", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "effb6f7d60c47e694fc6214f6af6532b698cb3755e4da530570318e0cec8f48a"}, {"source_id": "en85-u027-b0031", "target": "— Когда вспомню о нём, — сказала Агнес.", "source_sha256": "da8dc52640a4f65bcebfb50e8afb869064dbdfd914283f5b4f8e449f4757621c", "target_id": "ru-en85-u027-b0031", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "d648cef0be85bb5112d9dd16debc1c40a901c35c14a7180bdaab46d7a32ce047"}], "source_language": "English", "part": null, "book": null, "chapter": 25, "role": "chapter"}, "source_rows": [{"id": "en85-u027-b0032", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "She would have dismissed the subject so, but I was too full of it to allow that, and insisted on telling her how it happened that I had disgraced myself, and what chain of accidental circumstances had had the theatre for its final link. It was a great relief to me to do this, and to enlarge on the obligation that I owed to Steerforth for his care of me when I was unable to take care of myself.", "sha256": "f0af15a4427bd034b3d4a39c5f73684c9e2294ff61fe3543b5a9e136c087027f", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[32]/p[32]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u027-b0033", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘You must not forget,’ said Agnes, calmly changing the conversation as soon as I had concluded, ‘that you are always to tell me, not only when you fall into trouble, but when you fall in love. Who has succeeded to Miss Larkins, Trotwood?’", "sha256": "8586ad2499cf75f3f2222f7cf85e6d36d6c0781cedfa28949aa482fd49008b59", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[32]/p[33]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u027-b0034", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘No one, Agnes.’", "sha256": "c30fb0600b1d14bab264b3de4ba44e7412f4bf2ee8ebe2e85f10ad8aeffe7bbb", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[32]/p[34]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u027-b0035", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Someone, Trotwood,’ said Agnes, laughing, and holding up her finger.", "sha256": "634b3b73a6ad95ed60170aeae6890631c93db60d96d87b66956be07add21631d", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[32]/p[35]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u027-b0036", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘No, Agnes, upon my word! There is a lady, certainly, at Mrs. Steerforth’s house, who is very clever, and whom I like to talk to—Miss Dartle—but I don’t adore her.’", "sha256": "70e48392c25db84c006b138dac1f8b8d4b86a46e4520a6e56447b49a07495a50", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[32]/p[36]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u027-b0037", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Agnes laughed again at her own penetration, and told me that if I were faithful to her in my confidence she thought she should keep a little register of my violent attachments, with the date, duration, and termination of each, like the table of the reigns of the kings and queens, in the History of England. Then she asked me if I had seen Uriah.", "sha256": "7b19fe8a0b542569ba406f16af7cec4b1973f3a815d211b9c48bc64f4d910aef", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[32]/p[37]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u027-b0038", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Uriah Heep?’ said I. ‘No. Is he in London?’", "sha256": "b69f9d9e6e7f01ac12e967c9efe4cb47b125d4eb5e2190c60adc054944a2a246", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[32]/p[38]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u027-b0039", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘He comes to the office downstairs, every day,’ returned Agnes. ‘He was in London a week before me. I am afraid on disagreeable business, Trotwood.’", "sha256": "7fbf28615cf91bc45a89453af940cfbda5f6b8e0b19dd0b4ba8e8f02b4a9aa09", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[32]/p[39]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u027-b0040", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘On some business that makes you uneasy, Agnes, I see,’ said I. ‘What can that be?’", "sha256": "f840fdad0ece28aa3d4d643fb5f85da97b780359985c0e4cd916502eb48694b1", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[32]/p[40]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u027-b0041", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Agnes laid aside her work, and replied, folding her hands upon one another, and looking pensively at me out of those beautiful soft eyes of hers:", "sha256": "07e1c8b24a5645b5b5c755e0443d5743be47617e544de7ded09c407415f0825c", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[32]/p[41]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u027-b0042", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I believe he is going to enter into partnership with papa.’", "sha256": "2ffc22d3afcd5d499f7e936d47d7b1a4d7fa571431c32b5899477b7b339a1af4", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[32]/p[42]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u027-b0043", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘What? Uriah? That mean, fawning fellow, worm himself into such promotion!’ I cried, indignantly. ‘Have you made no remonstrance about it, Agnes? Consider what a connexion it is likely to be. You must speak out. You must not allow your father to take such a mad step. You must prevent it, Agnes, while there’s time.’", "sha256": "e92689b56ea45eaf9987a629d4ff6680a19c1a0b06f3d8c92b2c028df511d746", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[32]/p[43]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u027-b0044", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Still looking at me, Agnes shook her head while I was speaking, with a faint smile at my warmth: and then replied:", "sha256": "c958a92b02c631c42e74c1c19e980a3ccc68207b317d59709d0fa782ad101557", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[32]/p[44]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u027-b0045", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘You remember our last conversation about papa? It was not long after that—not more than two or three days—when he gave me the first intimation of what I tell you. It was sad to see him struggling between his desire to represent it to me as a matter of choice on his part, and his inability to conceal that it was forced upon him. I felt very sorry.’", "sha256": "16796eea85595f33d3926995373ee94758e8ea25a3d940ec45209d6411f68433", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[32]/p[45]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u027-b0046", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Forced upon him, Agnes! Who forces it upon him?’", "sha256": "5786a83df7b88555654ad585ee35c480b1b3238a98b60b6e10ba0209cd3b5d9c", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[32]/p[46]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u027-b0047", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Uriah,’ she replied, after a moment’s hesitation, ‘has made himself indispensable to papa. He is subtle and watchful. He has mastered papa’s weaknesses, fostered them, and taken advantage of them, until—to say all that I mean in a word, Trotwood,—until papa is afraid of him.’", "sha256": "b0112d55443d756679b852d53e585c1e2635b6b5b308a1b0c20b39384e78956e", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[32]/p[47]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u027-b0048", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "There was more that she might have said; more that she knew, or that she suspected; I clearly saw. I could not give her pain by asking what it was, for I knew that she withheld it from me, to spare her father. It had long been going on to this, I was sensible: yes, I could not but feel, on the least reflection, that it had been going on to this for a long time. I remained silent.", "sha256": "59bab28b68625ec7638baf6c1b78c71d657c42f84336180c607ee7656418e6ff", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[32]/p[48]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u027-b0049", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘His ascendancy over papa,’ said Agnes, ‘is very great. He professes humility and gratitude—with truth, perhaps: I hope so—but his position is really one of power, and I fear he makes a hard use of his power.’", "sha256": "f8aad52b0d1d3079f5b51300d8c8d3cb04ff71c82ce5a57f78d627d6bb24dcd1", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[32]/p[49]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u027-b0050", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I said he was a hound, which, at the moment, was a great satisfaction to me.", "sha256": "8438282ce7dddfa189919170e7544aa0ed50d16036b1a0ef0cb15c114a9c420e", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[32]/p[50]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u027-b0051", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘At the time I speak of, as the time when papa spoke to me,’ pursued Agnes, ‘he had told papa that he was going away; that he was very sorry, and unwilling to leave, but that he had better prospects. Papa was very much depressed then, and more bowed down by care than ever you or I have seen him; but he seemed relieved by this expedient of the partnership, though at the same time he seemed hurt by it and ashamed of it.’", "sha256": "c5c1b7f6a86e35532c893c061d2ea48e5955952b5123f0364fc501264fed9acd", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[32]/p[51]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u027-b0052", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘And how did you receive it, Agnes?’", "sha256": "2bd4a2a7415c00ade78bb450aa8c13987dcac9888821ccf1acfc1877b9076790", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[32]/p[52]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u027-b0053", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I did, Trotwood,’ she replied, ‘what I hope was right. Feeling sure that it was necessary for papa’s peace that the sacrifice should be made, I entreated him to make it. I said it would lighten the load of his life—I hope it will!—and that it would give me increased opportunities of being his companion. Oh, Trotwood!’ cried Agnes, putting her hands before her face, as her tears started on it, ‘I almost feel as if I had been papa’s enemy, instead of his loving child. For I know how he has altered, in his devotion to me. I know how he has narrowed the circle of his sympathies and duties, in the concentration of his whole mind upon me. I know what a multitude of things he has shut out for my sake, and how his anxious thoughts of me have shadowed his life, and weakened his strength and energy, by turning them always upon one idea. If I could ever set this right! If I could ever work out his restoration, as I have so innocently been the cause of his decline!’", "sha256": "4104c115cc3804c84aae0a3bbbf418f0e30fc92301a95f4c1de152593bd044f4", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[32]/p[53]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u027-b0054", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I had never before seen Agnes cry. I had seen tears in her eyes when I had brought new honours home from school, and I had seen them there when we last spoke about her father, and I had seen her turn her gentle head aside when we took leave of one another; but I had never seen her grieve like this. It made me so sorry that I could only say, in a foolish, helpless manner, ‘Pray, Agnes, don’t! Don’t, my dear sister!’", "sha256": "16321baac022706feac5c03b89c2e8d6dfcbd4b751d0fc5845b1ef8282226409", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[32]/p[54]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u027-b0055", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "But Agnes was too superior to me in character and purpose, as I know well now, whatever I might know or not know then, to be long in need of my entreaties. The beautiful, calm manner, which makes her so different in my remembrance from everybody else, came back again, as if a cloud had passed from a serene sky.", "sha256": "9bd02a00afbc177f68a0bcf3fa32e1aac65a51420c1aded28397abe54053ba8c", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[32]/p[55]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u027-b0056", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘We are not likely to remain alone much longer,’ said Agnes, ‘and while I have an opportunity, let me earnestly entreat you, Trotwood, to be friendly to Uriah. Don’t repel him. Don’t resent (as I think you have a general disposition to do) what may be uncongenial to you in him. He may not deserve it, for we know no certain ill of him. In any case, think first of papa and me!’", "sha256": "bf1e9748582ebadbdbf8b4be79767e6b9f6a6f0a79afe86e823f52754f9c8b8a", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[32]/p[56]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u027-b0057", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Agnes had no time to say more, for the room door opened, and Mrs. Waterbrook, who was a large lady—or who wore a large dress: I don’t exactly know which, for I don’t know which was dress and which was lady—came sailing in. I had a dim recollection of having seen her at the theatre, as if I had seen her in a pale magic lantern; but she appeared to remember me perfectly, and still to suspect me of being in a state of intoxication.", "sha256": "0b32cfd9b107c307d4bcdd8006830793237ba755d5284f5d4ba1ce295de94009", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[32]/p[57]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u027-b0058", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Finding by degrees, however, that I was sober, and (I hope) that I was a modest young gentleman, Mrs. Waterbrook softened towards me considerably, and inquired, firstly, if I went much into the parks, and secondly, if I went much into society. On my replying to both these questions in the negative, it occurred to me that I fell again in her good opinion; but she concealed the fact gracefully, and invited me to dinner next day. I accepted the invitation, and took my leave, making a call on Uriah in the office as I went out, and leaving a card for him in his absence.", "sha256": "90ee60f1dba6957a7b062b4e6ba79ea0613938bd844ca11672b59e8671830bc5", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[32]/p[58]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u027-b0059", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "When I went to dinner next day, and on the street door being opened, plunged into a vapour-bath of haunch of mutton, I divined that I was not the only guest, for I immediately identified the ticket-porter in disguise, assisting the family servant, and waiting at the foot of the stairs to carry up my name. He looked, to the best of his ability, when he asked me for it confidentially, as if he had never seen me before; but well did I know him, and well did he know me. Conscience made cowards of us both.", "sha256": "4ca794e51e59d9a3abf202aa6929fd7ce6a05594d191c2735eaec486bc5da1df", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[32]/p[59]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u027-b0060", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I found Mr. Waterbrook to be a middle-aged gentleman, with a short throat, and a good deal of shirt-collar, who only wanted a black nose to be the portrait of a pug-dog. He told me he was happy to have the honour of making my acquaintance; and when I had paid my homage to Mrs. Waterbrook, presented me, with much ceremony, to a very awful lady in a black velvet dress, and a great black velvet hat, whom I remember as looking like a near relation of Hamlet’s—say his aunt.", "sha256": "7937a45597abe35da04529f8b46ef8f03cf186e5c5632bb250276ffa71666fe7", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[32]/p[60]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u027-b0061", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Mrs. Henry Spiker was this lady’s name; and her husband was there too: so cold a man, that his head, instead of being grey, seemed to be sprinkled with hoar-frost. Immense deference was shown to the Henry Spikers, male and female; which Agnes told me was on account of Mr. Henry Spiker being solicitor to something or to somebody, I forget what or which, remotely connected with the Treasury.", "sha256": "bc3bdb04fe1dda47cd7123952055508cba870a03b03706d497e253bdddc83782", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[32]/p[61]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u027-b0062", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I found Uriah Heep among the company, in a suit of black, and in deep humility. He told me, when I shook hands with him, that he was proud to be noticed by me, and that he really felt obliged to me for my condescension. I could have wished he had been less obliged to me, for he hovered about me in his gratitude all the rest of the evening; and whenever I said a word to Agnes, was sure, with his shadowless eyes and cadaverous face, to be looking gauntly down upon us from behind.", "sha256": "88249c0afaca382fd42d78d627631b7166f2f29d2c21462c11c61f4247dfe4f8", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[32]/p[62]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u027-b0063", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "There were other guests—all iced for the occasion, as it struck me, like the wine. But there was one who attracted my attention before he came in, on account of my hearing him announced as Mr. Traddles! My mind flew back to Salem House; and could it be Tommy, I thought, who used to draw the skeletons!", "sha256": "26b8b1baaf839adc82a110161e3524fcdd5b1a34cc5243b76de12e8031012206", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[32]/p[63]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}]}
